`enabledPlugins` below names a plugin AND the marketplace it comes from, and publishing a catalogue is not the same as registering one. `../.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` states what this repository OFFERS; nothing reads it on a session's behalf. `extraKnownMarketplaces` is what registers it, and without that block `archkeep@archkeep` names a marketplace no session has heard of.

Measured on Claude Code 2.1.239 with the block absent, which is how this repository shipped until the commit that added it: `claude plugin marketplace list` answers `No marketplaces configured`, `claude plugin details archkeep@archkeep` answers `not found`, and a session starts with none of the five arch-* skills and no language server. There is no warning line — the state is byte-for-byte a session that simply has no plugins, which is the silent direction `../AGENTS.md` refuses, in the repository whose own subject it is.

The source is a `directory` at `.` rather than the `github` source the same key also accepts. `.` is the repository root: a session reads this file only when it starts there, and that is the directory the path resolves against. A `github` entry would fetch the default branch instead, so a pull request that edits the language server or a skill would be reviewed by sessions still running the version before it — the argument `../.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`'s own note makes for shipping the plugin from the same commit as the code it acts on.

Claude Code follows a directory source to the live tree; it does not copy it. Codex does copy, which is why `../.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` carries the opposite warning.
